text: Jared Kushner publicly defended the controversial luxury tourism development near the Vjosa‑Narta lagoon, denying political favoritism and saying the €230 million land purchase was a private transaction; he said the project could bring €4 billion in investment and meet high environmental standards, Tirana Times reports.

sources.title: Jared Kushner Defends Controversial Albania Resort Project - Tirana Times
sources.articleText:
Trump’s son-in-law rejects allegations of preferential treatment, outlines plans for a €4 billion investment and addresses environmental concerns over the Zvërnec development.
Tirana Times, October 09, 2026 – Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of U.S. President Donald Trump, has issued his first extensive public defense of a controversial luxury tourism development in southern Albania, rejecting allegations of political favoritism and arguing that the proposed project could bring billions of euros in investment while meeting high environmental standards.
In a detailed statement released Thursday in response to an investigation by The New Yorker , Kushner said his business partners had purchased land near Zvërnec for €230 million in a private transaction, rather than receiving it from the Albanian government. He said the development, if approved and successfully completed, could generate approximately €4 billion in investment and create substantial economic opportunities.
Kushner’s response comes amid months of protests over the proposed development near the environmentally sensitive Vjosa-Narta lagoon, alongside questions concerning land ownership, government decisions and Albania’s environmental protection policies.
The controversy has attracted international attention partly because of Kushner’s family ties to Trump and his previous role as a senior White House adviser. Kushner has rejected suggestions that his Albanian business activities were intended to secure political advantages.
Kushner challenged claims that his investment group had benefited from favorable government decisions allowing development in protected coastal areas.
He said the property had been purchased from a private party for €230 million, describing the price as among the highest paid in the region for a comparable transaction. According to Kushner, legal advisers reviewed and verified the property title before the acquisition.
He described the project as a private commercial investment driven by confidence in Albania’s emerging tourism market, emphasizing that investors were committing substantial capital without guarantees of financial success.
Kushner said the investment group had spent more than three years and tens of millions of dollars studying the land, its environmental characteristics and the region’s development needs, while assembling international teams of architects, engineers, designers and environmental specialists.
He identified longtime business associate Asher Abehsera as a partner and chief executive responsible for daily management. Kushner said the Albanian Kastrati business family had initially brought the investment opportunity to his attention.
He also discussed the involvement of Ramez and Moutaz Alkhayyat, businessmen whom he first met in Doha during the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Kushner highlighted their experience in Qatar’s construction industry and their success in rebuilding their businesses after leaving Syria, where he said their property had been confiscated under the Assad government.
Kushner described himself as a minority partner without responsibility for daily operations. His personal involvement, he said, has focused primarily on the project’s architectural vision, design and selection of international partners.
He emphasized that the investment was intended to create more than a luxury resort, describing it as an opportunity to stimulate long-term economic activity and strengthen Albania’s position as an international tourism destination.
Addressing suggestions that the investment might have been facilitated to gain favor with Trump, Kushner argued that the chronology contradicted such interpretations.
He said his interest in the project began in the summer of 2021, when he was acting as a private citizen and before Trump announced his campaign to return to the White House.
Kushner similarly rejected suggestions that Albanian officials approved the nearby airport development at his request. He said the airport project had already received approval when he first became acquainted with the investment opportunity and that its existence was one of the factors attracting him to the region.
His explanation directly addresses allegations of political influence, although broader questions concerning development decisions, environmental protection and the role of public authorities remain part of the debate.
Although Kushner maintains that the land was acquired through a legitimate private transaction, the ownership of parts of the proposed development site has faced legal scrutiny in Albania.
In July, Reuters reported that Albanian prosecutors were investigating businessman Artur Shehu, who had sold coastal property to a company connected with the development, over suspicions involving falsified property documents, drug trafficking and money laundering.
According to case files reviewed by Reuters, prosecutors suspected that some land involved had been acquired using forged documents. Shehu has denied the allegations.
Reuters reported no indication that Kushner or his business partners were aware of the alleged irregularities.
Local residents have also challenged ownership claims involving property included in the proposed development area, asserting that land belonging to their families had been improperly transferred to others.
The allegations remain subject to legal proceedings, and no conclusion about the validity of the disputed ownership claims can be drawn solely from the investigations.
Kushner’s assertion that the investment group paid €230 million and obtained legal verification of ownership is an important part of his defense. However, the private nature of the transaction does not independently resolve allegations concerning earlier ownership transfers.
Environmental protection represents another major element of Kushner’s response.
